summary: The new experiment ran clean and answered the question on its own terms. With the automatic transfer never called, one explicit `LeadershipTransferToServer` naming the demoted member returned an empty error in 0 ms, the named member never reported Leader and ended as a non-voter, the cluster had six leaderless samples in 475, and the maximum term rose from two to four; the same single request naming an ordinary voter installed that voter with no leaderless sample and one term advance. Because only the target's suffrage varies between the two cases, that contrast lets the account attribute the leaderless interval and the extra term advance to the request itself, which is exactly what the earlier source finding had forced it to withdraw. I restored the disruption attribution in the counterevidence with those measured numbers, rewrote the limitation to state the measurement and its caveats (one run, one container, 50 ms in-memory timeouts, no per-member term sampling across the window, so the split between the failed election round and the adopted term is not separated), appended the parsed events to the rationale, and recorded the joint history that ties this experiment to the flag probe and demotion race. I also reissued both transfer knowledge entries at revision 11 with the new receipt added to their execution sets, so the premises about the explicit-target lookup and the non-voter candidate's term adoption now carry it. The conclusion stays violated with the scoped defect asserted, and the interpretation's recorded execution moves to this experiment since the receipt is now its own.
